newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end off lows as dollar perks up.
newsitem.headline: German shares end off lows as dollar perks up.

text.p: German shares fell on Thursday amid pressure from overnight Wall Street losses and a sliding dollar, but picked up from their lows in post-bourse trade as the U.S. currency perked up in the afternoon.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 65.59 points, or two percent, at 3,349.81 points but the IBIS DAX index, which tracks post-bourse trade, staged a minor recovery to close the day at 3,367.82 points.
Traders said the drop may be the start of a long-awaited market correction in response to the recent heady gains, including a 20 percent rise in the DAX in the last 10 weeks.
"It's healthy and not much of a worry," one trader said.
"The drop is pretty much in line with what a lot of people have been expecting for some time," the Frankfurt trader said. "This should help make the market a bit more attractive."

Chemical shares remained in the spotlight as Hoechst AG kept up its decline from Wednesday tied to disappointment over its shelving of plans to list its Hoechst Marion Roussel pharmaceuticals unit on the bourse.
Hoechst shares, which fell 10 percent on Wednesday, ended bourse trade down 1.65 marks at 68.80 marks, inching off their lows in later trade to close the IBIS session at 69.25 marks.
Other chemical sector shares, including Bayer AG, BASF AG and Schering AG, were all also under pressure.

Shares in engineering group Deutz AG slumped as much as 1.75 marks to 12 marks on profit-taking before ending bourse trade down 85 pfennigs at 12.90 marks and slipping to 12.80 marks in post-bourse trade.

Deutz was under pressure after surging in recent days after a report in Germany's Platow Brief saying the company, formerly known as Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, would return to a profit this year. Deutz plans to release its results on May 15.
